### (c)

```{r 2_1_3}
mod_budget <- lm(Visits ~ Budget, data = web)
mod_adtype <- lm(Visits ~ AdType, data = web)
mod_full <- lm(Visits ~ Budget + AdType, data = web)

summary(mod_full)
anova(mod_budget, mod_full)
anova(mod_adtype, mod_full)
```

AdType does appear to be significant. Budget does not appear to be significant.

### (b)

I added in a grid to start over to demonstrate the change point where it starts converging to the different peaks. 

```{r 2_2_2}
multi_modal <- function(x) {
    # Parameters for the first peak
    mean1 <- -2
    sd1 <- 1
    peak1 <- dnorm(x, mean = mean1, sd = sd1)

    # Parameters for the second peak
    mean2 <- 2
    sd2 <- .5
    peak2 <- dnorm(x, mean = mean2, sd = sd2)

    # Sum of both peaks
    peak1 + peak2
}

start <- seq(-2.5, 2.5, by = .1)
end <- unlist(lapply(start, \(x) optim(x, multi_modal, method = "L-BFGS-B", control = list(fnscale = -1))$par))

ggplot(NULL, aes(x = start, y = end)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "Start Position", y = "End Estimate")
```

### (b)

```{r 2_3_2}
resids <- residuals(gam_mod)
resids <- as.data.frame(x = resids)
ggplot(data = resids, aes(x=resids)) + 
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density))) + 
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, color = "red", linewidth = 1.2)
ks.test(resids$resids, "pnorm")
```

### (c)

```{r 2_3_3}
res_squared <- residuals(gam_mod)^2
aux_mod <- lm(res_squared ~ Budget + AdType, data = web)

bp <- bptest(aux_mod) 
p_val <- bp$p.value
p_label <- paste("BP Test p-value:", format.pval(p_val, digits = 3))

fits <- fitted(gam_mod, what = "mu")
ggplot(NULL, aes(x = fits, y = resids$resids)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "fitted", y = "resids") + 
    annotate("text", x = median(fits), y = Inf, label = p_label, vjust = 1.5, color = "blue")
```

### (d)

```{r 2_3_4}
# R-squared-ish formula
cor(web$Visits, fitted(gam_mod, what = "mu"))^2
```

### (e)

```{r 2_3_5}
cross_validate <- function(fold_num) { 
    train_dt <- web[folds != fold_num, ]
    val_dt <- web[folds == fold_num, ]
    cv_mod <- gamlss(Visits ~ Budget + AdType, sigma.formula = ~ Budget, data = train_dt, trace = FALSE, environment = environment())
    preds <- predict(cv_mod, what = "mu", data = train_dt, newdata = val_dt, type = "response")
    raw_resids <- val_dt$Visits - preds
    rmse <- sqrt(mean(raw_resids^2))
    rmse
}

set.seed(1337)
K <- 25
folds <- rep(1:K, length = nrow(web)) %>% #Rep K folds n times
    sample()
## Using sapply()
rmse_results <- sapply(1:K, FUN=cross_validate)

## Plot the Results
ggplot() + 
    geom_density(mapping=aes(x=rmse_results))
```

# HW 2.4

### (a)

```{r 2_4_1_1}
mod <- gamlss(formula = Visits ~ Budget + AdType, sigma.formula = ~Budget, data = web)
summary(mod)
```

Looking at the initial summary output, we see that the p-value for Budget is almost 0 (< 2e-16). Due to this, we conclude that Budget does have a significant effect on the number of visists. 

```{r 2_4_1_2}
mu_cis <- confint(mod, what = "mu", level = 0.95)

# Convert it into a clean table structure
mu_cis_table <- data.frame(
  Beta_Estimate = coef(mod, what = "mu"),
  "2.5%"      = mu_cis[, 1],
  "97.5%"      = mu_cis[, 2]
)

print(mu_cis_table)
```

### (b) 

```{r 2_4_2}
mod_no_ad <- gamlss(formula = Visits ~ Budget, sigma.formula = ~Budget, data = web)
LR.test(mod_no_ad, mod)
```

Due to the p-value of .94 we conclude that the reduced model performs as well as the full model, implying that AdType does not have a significant effect on the number of visits. 

### (c)

```{r 2_4_3}
sigma_cis <- confint(mod, what = "sigma", level = 0.95)
sigma_cis
```

### (d)

```{r 2_4_4}
budget_vals <- min(web$Budget):max(web$Budget)
pred_vals <- data.frame(Budget = budget_vals)

budget_preds <- predictAll(mod_no_ad, data = web, newdata = pred_vals, type = "response")

lower_90 <- qNO(0.05, mu = budget_preds$mu, sigma = budget_preds$sigma)
upper_90 <- qNO(0.95, mu = budget_preds$mu, sigma = budget_preds$sigma)

# 3. Combine them into a clean data frame with your predictions
budget_intervals <- data.frame(
    budget = budget_vals,
    fit   = budget_preds$mu,
    lower = lower_90,
    upper = upper_90
)

ggplot(data = budget_intervals, aes(x = budget, y = fit)) + 
    geom_point(data = web, aes(x = Budget, y = Visits), color = "black") + 
    geom_line(color = "red", lwd = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(y = lower), color = "blue", lwd = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(y = upper), color = "blue", lwd = 2) + 
    labs(x = "Budget", y = "Visits") +
    theme_minimal()
```
